topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the opening framing and learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Conventional modalities in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine primary standard interventions aimed at physically removing or non-selectively damaging tumor tissue along with their clinical limitations.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cell-cycle, signaling, and repair vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that selectively exploit specific molecular dependencies and genetic defects inherent to cancer cells.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of treatment resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore oncogene addiction, small-molecule kinase targeting, and the molecular pathways driving therapy resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the development and mechanisms of action of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the basis of immune surveillance and modern clinical approaches designed to activate and engineer T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Long-term progress, clinical challenges, and future perspectives in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad historical trends in survival, current hurdles in precision oncology, and emerging ethical dilemmas in cancer management.
